title: Evictor Watchdog + OOM Stall-Breaker: coordinated runtime patch for cross-env KV fragmentation
creator: Marco Alvarez
description: Customer escalations over the last two weeks revealed a recurring pattern: large bursty workloads (chat-heavy) on hosted and dedicated fleets cause long-tail memory fragmentation and emergent KV-cache object retention. Symptoms: GPU OOM spikes under sustained throughput, high slab imbalance, and slow compaction that prevents timely reclamation. This ticket implements a coordinated runtime patch comprised of an Evictor Watchdog, an OOM Stall-Breaker behavior, and a conservative per-tenant slab reservation to safely lower OOM frequency while preserving SLAs.
incident_summary: Between 2026-02-18 and 2026-02-26 three customers reported 5+ OOM-driven failures each on hosted and dedicated pools. Private customers also surfaced similar fragmentation regressions after long-lived sessions. Investigation traced the failures to fragmentation coupled with stale KV index tombstones that prevented compaction from reclaiming hot prefix caches rapidly enough under bursts.
root_cause: Runtime allocator fragmentation + KV-index tombstone accumulation. Under sustained bursts, eviction heuristics failed to prioritize long-tail KV objects that created slab starvation for new transient allocations. Compaction runs are rate-limited and sometimes deferred; combined with cross-tenant metadata skew this led to per-GPU peak memory pressure and OOMs.
mitigation_summary: 1) Evictor Watchdog: background controller that detects slab imbalance thresholds and accelerates targeted compaction for affected slab classes. 2) OOM Stall-Breaker: graceful request backpressure that demotes oversized KV entries to tombstones and forces small synchronous compaction for the impacted tenant during recovery windows. 3) Per-tenant soft-reservation: short-lived slab reservations for critical system allocations under burst to prevent complete starvation. These are conservative defaults that trade a small amount of throughput headroom for robustness.
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (canary): deploy to 10% of hosted fleet and one dedicated pilot cluster; enable watch-dog in observe-only mode for 24h and collect metrics. Stage 2: enable auto-corrective compaction with OOM Stall-Breaker at 25% fleet, run for 48h. Stage 3: full rollout after validation +/- toggle for private customers (requires opt-in and ops coordination). Rollback path: disable auto-correct and revert to observe-only within 30 minutes; emergency throttle to reduce burst capacity if OOMs reappear.
monitoring_checks: Dashboard: per-tenant slab usage, tombstone ratio, compaction time-series
